title: Obama Pledges Economic Aid to India, but Says Trade Barriers Remain
main_content:
U.S. President Barack Obama has pledged $4 billion in American investments and loans to India, but said trade between the world’s two largest democracies is still marked by “so much untapped potential.”

On the second day of a three-day visit to India, Obama told a business conference attended by U.S. and Indian corporate executives there are “still too many barriers, hoops to jump through” in completing deals between the two countries. He noted that bilateral U.S.-India trade totals only $100 billion annually, less than a fifth of American business deals with Chinese companies.

Rain did little to dampen the excitement around President Barack Obama’s landmark visit to India as thousands of troops took part in a dazzling military parade Monday where he was the guest of honor.

Obama is the first U.S. president to attend India’s Republic Day, which celebrates its first constitution as an independent state, taking effect on January 26, 1950.

The U.S. president spent the first day of his three-day visit Sunday bonding with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and sealing a clutch of deals.

questions.question: What did Barack Obama say about the trade relations between the USA and India?
options: They are characterized by strong collaboration and high efficiency.
They face significant challenges due to numerous barriers.
They are thriving and meeting all expectations.
They have surpassed trade relations with other countries.
questions.answer: They face significant challenges due to numerous barriers.

questions.question: How do the US-India trade exchanges compare to those between the US and China?
options: The US-India trade is nearly equal to that with China.
US-India trade is significantly lower than US-China trade.
US-India trade is higher than US-China trade.
They are both at a standstill with no significant difference.
questions.answer: US-India trade is significantly lower than US-China trade.

questions.question: What does India’s Republic Day celebrate?
options: The establishment of the Indian Parliament.
The signing of the Declaration of Independence.
The introduction of the Indian National Anthem.
The adoption of its first constitution as an independent state.
questions.answer: The adoption of its first constitution as an independent state.
